title: Govt approves Rs 86 crore support for Peptris' AI-driven drug development programme
key_facts: India's Technology Development Board (TDB), under the Department of Science and Technology, signed an agreement with Peptris Technologies Pvt Ltd to provide Rs 86 crore under the Research Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund for an AI-led drug development programme, according to an official statement on Monday (12 Oct 2026).
The project is called VIGOR: Advancing AI-Discovered Molecules from Bench to Clinic; its total cost is Rs 172 crore.
It aims to advance four drug candidates from Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 4 to TRL 6 through preclinical development, validation and preparation for clinical trials.
The financial support will be given through Optionally Convertible Debt (OCD).
The four candidates are PEPR111 (neuromuscular disorders and oncology), PEPRX101 (alopecia), PEPR202 (neuropathy) and PEPR112 (Duchenne muscular dystrophy).

The three-year programme covers advanced preclinical studies, IND-enabling studies (work needed before a regulator allows human trials), formulation development, and clinical trial preparation and initiation, subject to regulatory and scientific requirements.
TDB Secretary Rajesh Kumar Pathak said sustained investment and scientific validation are required to turn promising discoveries into therapeutic candidates.
quote_evidence: The project aims to advance four drug candidates from Technology Readiness Level (TRL)-4 to TRL-6 through preclinical development, validation and preparation for clinical trials.
Financial support will be provided through Optionally Convertible Debt (OCD).
The government said that the project is intended to help bridge the gap between AI-based discovery and clinical development
why_it_matters_hint: A government development fund is backing, with repayable financing, a three-year push to move four AI-discovered drug candidates toward clinical trials; none is yet in trials.
event_date: Statement issued Monday 12 Oct 2026; signing date not stated
notes: Read in full via IANS (fulltext). IANS wrote the piece from an official ministry statement (Ministry of Science and Technology), so IANS is credited and the ministry named. Rs 86 crore is half of the stated Rs 172 crore total; the article does not say who pays the other half. Candidate names are from the statement.
